lots.what_it_is: Pair of moulded frosted pressed-glass clam shell wall light shades with a pale amber/yellow tint, each held by clips in a gold-painted pressed steel half-round backplate (catalogued '1920S SHELL STYLE WALL SCONCES'). English-style art deco clam shell type, 1930s style; maker unknown.
lots.condition: Glass looks whole in both photos with no obvious chips on the wavy rims, but the rims are only seen at low resolution. Backplates are gold paint over bare steel with wear; inside of one backplate shows bare metal, wire clips and a cable hole, but no lampholder or wiring is visible. Yellow tint could be original colour or nicotine/dust staining.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: both shades from the front, matching ribbed shell moulding. The small white sticker on the left shade is a handwritten lot/tally sticker, not a maker label (cropped and enlarged). Photo 2: one shade from above showing the steel backplate interior, glass retained by bent tabs, a central cable hole, no lampholder seen. No moulded maker mark visible in either photo.

lots.guide_summary: Only one close entry survives: a single clam shell wall light with fitting and wires sold for $60 hammer at Gowans (listed 2026-03-30). That is 1 sold, 0 unsold, 0 asking. A pair might fairly be worth up to about twice that, but no pair sale was found to prove it. Seven other Gowans lighting results ($20 to $200 hammer) are kept as category guides only. All AUD, no conversion.
lots.working: Keep: lowest surviving close SOLD = $60 hammer (single clam shell light, 2026-03-30, within 24 months). Treating the pair as worth at least one single: 60 / 1.198 = 50.08, round down to $50 hammer (all-in $59.90). Flip: conservative resale = $60 (the only sold evidence) less about 13.4% selling fees ($8) and about $25 to pack and post fragile glass = $27; 27 / 2.396 = 11.27, round down to $10. If you believe the pair resells at 2 x $60 = $120: (120 - 16 - 25) / 2.396 = 32.97, so $30, but that doubling is not proven. Premium 19.8%; pickup Moonah, inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: Type is clear from the photos and there is one good close SOLD result whose page and photo I opened, but no maker mark was read, the underside and rims are not fully seen, and fittings are unknown. Only one sold comparable and it was a single.
lots.question_for_gowans: Are there any chips or cracks on the wavy rims or around the fixing tabs? Is there a moulded maker mark on either glass? Do they still have lampholders and wiring, or are they shades and backplates only?
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped: lot 423637 'PAIR OF BRASS WALL SCONCES WITH BULBS & REMOTE CONTROLS' $220 hammer (listed 2026-07-12): modern brass lights with remotes, not comparable. All other researcher entries confirmed on the API page (titles, cents, bid counts and dates match). Lot 400382 upgraded from category guide to close after I opened its photo and found it is a single frosted glass clam shell wall light. Current-sale lot 442518 (PAIR OF ART DECO LIGHT FITTINGS) excluded.

lots.what_it_is: Single large raw live-edge timber slab catalogued 'SLAB OF MORETON BAY CHESTNUT' (Castanospermum australe, also called black bean), one of four chestnut slabs, lots 1107 to 1110.
lots.condition: Raw, sawn and unfinished, appears dried. A split runs down from the top end for roughly a quarter to a third of the length, through a knot. Wavy live edge with some fibrous bark remnants. No dimensions given; it looks about 1.6 to 2 m tall leaning on a roller door, but that is a guess.
lots.key_photo_findings: Cream sapwood with brown heartwood stripes and a knot near the top, a long split from the top end down past the knot, chalk '1109 9/10/26' and a round lot sticker. Pale colour and grain fit Moreton Bay chestnut, but species cannot be proven from a photo. Neighbouring slabs 1108 and 1110 shown either side.

lots.working: No SOLD result for the same species, so under the rules both maximum bids are 0. For orientation only (not a maximum bid): the close camphor laurel results put a slab like this at about $15 to $55 hammer, and $55 / 1.198 = $45.91, so about $45 would be the most the local evidence would justify if you accepted camphor laurel as a stand-in. No flip margin: resale of a raw slab of unknown size, less fees and freight, would not double the buy price on this evidence. Premium 19.8%; pickup Moonah, inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: Species is the catalogue's word only, no dimensions or thickness, and no same-species sale exists; all evidence is other timbers.
lots.question_for_gowans: What are the length, width and thickness? Is it air dried (how long) or freshly milled, and how was the species identified? How far does the top split run, and is there any borer or rot in the sapwood?
lots.dropped_entries: Researcher for this lot said the chestnut run was lots 1108 to 1111; the silky oak lot 442691 photo shows chalk '1111', so it is 1107 to 1110. Researcher's mixed entry '2 SLABS OF WALNUT $40; $45 hammer (2 slabs of Tasmanian-type oak $20)' is garbled: the page shows 2 SLABS OF WALNUT $40 (1 bid), 2 SLABS OF TEA TREE $20 (0 bids), 2 SLABS OF MARITIME PINE $20 (0 bids); there is no $45 oak lot. Dropped as written. The 'Huon pine median $55 / blackheart sassafras median $40' aggregate and the huon pine 2- and 3-slab lots are confirmed but dropped as entries: premium Tasmanian species, not comparable. 4 SLABS OF KING BILLY PINE $200 and 8 BLACKWOOD SLABS $230 dropped (multi-slab lots).
